title: Grateful Dead Live at Roscoe Maples Pavilion, Stanford U. on 1973-02-09
lineage: SBD> MR> REEL> DAT> SS> CDR> DAW (Bertha)> CDA

ai_review.summary: Rough‑but‑lovable soundboard capture of the historic 2/9/73 show – crisp remix highlights a high‑energy set packed with first‑time classics.
ai_review.review: The February 9, 1973 recording is a soundboard source that was originally rough and crunchy but has been expertly remixed by Jay Ashley, delivering clear, punchy audio despite occasional bite‑yness or pitch quirks. Musically the concert is a landmark – the band rolls out a slew of debut performances (Eyes of the World, China Doll, Here Comes Sunshine, Row Jimmy, Loose Lucy, etc.) with soaring energy and tight transitions, especially the Truckin'→Eyes→China Doll sequence.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4‑5 stars; comments praise both the historic setlist and the high‑quality remix, outweighing minor technical complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Original board tape is rough, crunchy and a bit bitey; the Ashley remaster cleans up clarity, balances mix, but some users note slight pitch drift or occasional drop‑outs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Aggressive first set that settles into a smooth groove, followed by a second‑set jam marathon; seamless transitions (e.g., Truckin' → Eyes → China Doll) and a high‑spirited encore make the flow feel like a celebratory debut.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers highlight Jerry's guitar tone as 'true to live', 'crunchy' in a good way, and even call him a 'mad bastardo' on El Paso; his playing is consistently praised throughout.
